Population increased in Windsor and Maidenhead

The estimated population of Windsor and Maidenhead in 2024 was 158,943 usual residents, a rise of 1.1% since 2023.

This meant that Windsor and Maidenhead's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Windsor and Maidenhead increased by 3.3%.

Over this slightly longer period, Windsor and Maidenhead was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Windsor and Maidenhead

The average (median) age rose to 42.7 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Windsor and Maidenhead has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Windsor and Maidenhead is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Windsor and Maidenhead's population of 158,943 usual residents was made up of:

  • 30,120 people aged 0 to 15 years, (19%)
  • 98,854 people aged 16 to 64 years, (62.2%)
  • 29,969 people aged 65 years and over, (18.9%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Windsor and Maidenhead has a similar proportion of people in these age categories.

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Windsor and Maidenhead, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Windsor and Maidenhead
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Windsor and Maidenhead, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 44 people (0%). In total, there were 1,353 births and 1,309 deaths in Windsor and Maidenhead.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 313 (0.2%). There were 11,130 people entering the area and 10,817 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Windsor and Maidenhead's population of 1,465 (0.9%) as a result of 2,632 people entering the area and 1,167 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Windsor and Maidenhead was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Windsor and Maidenhead in mid-2023 is 157,174.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 760 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 1,175 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 1,935 people.
